title: Negative (interim): active polar thin-film drops from a noisy film never give persistent motile daughters at 128-256^2; mild activity coarsens the drops, strong extensile stress with surface coupling turns the film into a writhing fission-fusion foam
summary: Campaign step on Q:thin-film-active-drops with the sighting's world (lubrication, wetting, polar order, polarization-surface coupling chpa, active stress ca, self-propulsion mu0). Eight labkit packs at 128^2 over mu0 0-0.004, chpa 0-0.2, ca 0-0.3 show 0-1 persistent splits, merges equal to or above splits, at most 4.6 body lengths travelled, and coarsening to 1-5 bodies by t=4000. Two 256^2 runs with a thicker film (h0 3, chpa 0.2, ca 0.2/0.3) become an active-turbulent foam of 5-12 ridges that pinch and fuse continuously, not discrete drops. Thin-film drops coalesce on contact, so whatever splits re-merges. Persistent daughters need either larger drops (Stegemerten et al. 2022 used V~7e4 on 800^2) or a mechanism that keeps daughters apart (opposite polarization). Neither was reached here.

finding.operator: active stress -ca pp plus polarization-surface coupling and self-propulsion in a dewetting thin film
finding.control: Laplacian twin in the sighting (no drops at all); passive film (static drops)
finding.result: persistent splits 0-1 in 8/8 packs at 128^2 (merges >= splits in 5/8); 256^2 h0 3: 5-12 fusing ridges, no discrete drops
